About Me

About Me

I am a final-year Software Engineering (Cybersecurity) student at the University of Technology Sydney with a strong passion for building secure, scalable, and user-focused technology. My interest in engineering began with a curiosity about how digital systems work behind the scenes, from mobile apps to cloud platforms and evolved into a commitment to developing solutions that are both innovative and reliable.

Throughout my degree, I have developed a strong foundation in software engineering, cybersecurity, and AI-driven systems, while maintaining a high academic performance and actively seeking opportunities to apply my skills in real-world environments.

During my internship at a fast-paced startup, I worked across software testing, frontend development, and code migration, gaining hands-on experience in React, Next.js, debugging, and agile collaboration. I learned how to adapt quickly, solve problems independently, and contribute meaningfully within a team environment.

Combined with my experience in iOS development, hackathon projects, tutoring, and peer leadership roles, I am building a professional identity as an adaptable, technically strong, and team-oriented engineer who thrives in dynamic environments and continuously seeks growth.

Internship Reflection

Reflection on Internship

What were your expectations about your internship before you joined? +

Before beginning my internship, I expected a structured environment where I would be assigned a well-defined set of technical tasks aligned with my role as a software engineering intern. I anticipated working primarily on coding-related responsibilities within a clear framework, with specific deliverables and minimal deviation from my assigned tasks.

I thought my experience would largely involve implementing features, debugging pre-existing code, and following established processes.

What was the reality? How was it different from your expectations? +

The reality was significantly different because I joined a dynamic startup environment where flexibility, adaptability, and initiative were crucial. Rather than focusing solely on a predefined set of coding tasks, I was required to work across multiple areas of the business.

Initially, I conducted detailed testing of the company's website and mobile application. I identified bugs, documented them carefully, and reported them using Microsoft Teams and Trello via structured tickets. This experience sharpened my attention to detail, reinforced the importance of clear documentation, and improved my ability to communicate technical issues effectively.

Later, I contributed to frontend design improvements using Lovable AI and took on the challenge of migrating React-based code into the company's Next.js codebase. This migration was technically complex due to differences between frameworks and minor compatibility issues that required careful debugging. I applied the software engineering concepts and coding skills I have learned at university, such as modular design, version control, and systematic debugging, to independently resolve these issues. I also leveraged Beyond Compare (software) to efficiently manage the migration. Collaborative testing sessions with the team further strengthened my confidence in teamwork, problem-solving, and communication in real-world conditions.

Overall, the internship was far more dynamic and unpredictable than I initially expected. However, this unpredictability allowed me to gain broader exposure, deepen my technical skills, and also develop my soft skills. It also gave me the opportunity to directly apply the knowledge and skills I have learned through my university studies in a professional setting.

What lessons were the most important from your internship? Why were they important? +

The most important lessons I learned were adaptability, proactive problem-solving, and effective communication. Working in a startup taught me that engineers must be flexible and ready to step outside their comfort zones. I realized that technical skills alone are not sufficient, and clear documentation, structured reporting, and collaboration are equally critical for success in real-world projects.

Additionally, understanding the differences between React and Next.js improved my ability to learn new frameworks quickly. This skill is essential in an industry where technology evolves rapidly, and the ability to self-learn ensures long-term career growth. The internship also reinforced the value of attention to detail, iterative testing, and the importance of balancing speed with accuracy in a fast-paced work environment.

After your workplace experience, what would you say your value proposition would be to an employer? How can you demonstrate this? +

My value proposition is that I am an adaptable, technically capable engineer who can contribute across testing, frontend development, debugging, and collaborative workflows. I am confident in both independent problem-solving and team-based projects, and I can thrive in environments that require flexibility and quick learning. I can demonstrate this value through tangible outputs such as documented bug reports, contributions to code migrations, GitHub repositories showcasing my projects, and practical experience working in agile, fast-moving startup settings. I can also show how I have successfully applied my university-learned software and engineering skills to solve real-world technical challenges.

How did your internship influence the type of role in which you are interested? +

My internship reinforced my interest in software engineering roles that combine technical depth with collaborative problem-solving. I discovered that I enjoy roles where I can work across the full stack, from testing and frontend development to debugging and system integration, while contributing to team-oriented projects. It also highlighted my interest in cybersecurity-focused work, as I became more aware of the importance of secure coding practices, careful testing, and managing vulnerabilities.

Going forward, I am particularly interested in joining innovative and fast-moving teams where continuous learning, adaptability, and cross-functional contributions are valued. This internship solidified my desire for roles where I can apply both the technical expertise I have developed at university and my collaborative skills to solve meaningful, real-world problems.

Cover Letter

Application — Industrus Engineering Graduate Program

Prathamesh Ahire  ·  prathamesh.ahire1204@gmail.com  ·  0413 525 573

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to apply for the Industrus Engineering Graduate Program, having recently completed my Software Engineering (Cybersecurity) degree at the University of Technology Sydney. With hands-on internship experience across software testing, frontend development, and agile delivery, combined with a GPA of 6/7, I am confident in my ability to contribute meaningfully to your team from day one. Please find my responses to the selection criteria below.

A commitment to ethical conduct and the highest standards of professional accountability

During my internship at Tipaload Pty Ltd, I was responsible for end-to-end testing of the company's web and mobile platforms ahead of a major product release. When I discovered critical bugs, including a broken truck registration dialog that prevented users from completing carrier sign-up, I documented each issue with precise reproduction steps, severity labels, and screenshots before logging structured Trello tickets and reporting through Microsoft Teams. Rather than minimising severity, I flagged every issue transparently, even when this created additional work. My thorough reporting enabled the team to resolve several high-priority defects before release, directly protecting platform stability and the company's reputation.

Demonstrated ability to effectively communicate both with other engineers and with stakeholders from different fields

At Tipaload, I needed to communicate technical findings clearly to both engineers and non-technical product stakeholders. I adapted my communication by writing structured Trello tickets tailored to a mixed audience and providing real-time verbal briefings to the engineering team on complex issues. In parallel, my tutoring role at Ezy Math required me to translate difficult mathematical and scientific concepts for students from Year 5 to Year 12, further sharpening my ability to adjust my communication style to suit different audiences. As a result, the team was able to triage and resolve issues efficiently because every stakeholder understood the nature and priority of each bug.

The ability to engage with a creative, innovative and proactive environment

At Tipaload, my supervisor identified the carrier sign-up flow as a priority for visual improvement but had no solution in place. I independently explored and leveraged Lovable AI to prototype and implement frontend design improvements, then took on the technically complex challenge of migrating the React-based components into the company's Next.js codebase. Faced with framework compatibility issues, I used Beyond Compare to manage structural differences and resolved conflicts independently before presenting the solution to the team. The improved interface was successfully adopted into the production codebase.

Demonstrated ability to use and manage information

The React-to-Next.js migration at Tipaload required me to systematically manage a large volume of technical information across two codebases. I used Beyond Compare to perform a structured analysis, tracking which components needed modification, which could transfer directly, and which contained incompatibilities requiring resolution. I maintained a clear record of changes at each stage and kept version control up to date throughout via GitHub. The migration was completed with no data loss and no broken functionality.

The ability to manage your own performance in a professional environment

Tipaload operated as a fast-moving startup with no rigid task structure, requiring me to deliver independently across testing, bug reporting, frontend design, and code migration simultaneously. I structured my own workload by establishing daily priorities and communicating progress regularly through Trello sprint updates. When I encountered unfamiliar frameworks, I proactively upskilled through documentation rather than waiting for direction, including self-teaching Next.js integration patterns. I delivered on all workstreams concurrently and was given progressively more complex tasks as the internship progressed.

A demonstrated ability to work as part of a team and to show leadership when required

During the Apple Foundation Program, I was placed in a cross-functional team to design, prototype, and build an original iOS application called Singular within a four-week sprint. I actively contributed to daily stand-ups and UI architecture decisions. When the team encountered integration conflicts between independently developed modules near the deadline, I stepped up to coordinate a technical resolution session, mapped the conflicts, and guided the team through a structured debugging process to unblock the project. The team delivered a polished, fully functional app on time, which was well-received at the final program showcase.

I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my skills and experience align with the Industrus Engineering Graduate Program. Please feel free to contact me at prathamesh.ahire1204@gmail.com or on 0413 525 573.

I look forward to hearing from you.

Kind Regards,
